content.title: About
content.content: Crab sushi is a roll made of vinegared rice, nori, and fresh crab meat, often complemented with avocado, cucumber, and soy sauce. The crab adds a delicate sea flavor and subtle sweetness, while the rice provides a soft texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crab meat in sushi is often used as real crab, though many restaurants serve imitation crab (surimi).
Sushi originated in Southeast Asia and became popular in Japan in the 17th century.
Nori sheets are rich in iodine and B‑vitamins.
Traditional sushi is served with soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Crab meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: A single roll typically contains 150–250 kcal, making it a good option for weight management.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Crab is a good source of zinc, selenium, and copper, which support immune function and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Crab contains polyunsaturated fats beneficial for heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Crab provides vitamin B12, important for the nervous system and blood formation.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to crab.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce and pickled ingredients can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Potential toxins
items.content: Improperly handled crab can harbor bacteria or toxins that cause food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sushi is typically eaten with chopsticks, dipped lightly in soy sauce. Add a dab of wasabi for heat and ginger between pieces to cleanse the palate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared sushi in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, freezing is possible, though the rice texture may change.
